facts: Inside a multiplexer `TERM_PROGRAM` names the multiplexer, so the emulator's own markers are the fallback; over ssh only `TERM` and `LC_TERMINAL` usually survive. `other` is a terminal nothing here identifies.
A Windows console that names no other terminal. Over ssh the client's terminal is unknowable, so that stays `other`.
Emulators that render OSC 8 hyperlinks. Absent here means unknown, not "no": `windows_console` may be Windows Terminal (links) or conhost (none), and Konsole renders them only when a setting is on.
The wrapper's bin names: the npm package's `bin` entries.
PATH entries scanned for the wrapper, so a pathological PATH stays cheap.

The wrapper the shell would run, found as `which` would find it: the first PATH entry holding one of `names` (with Windows' shim extensions), symlinks resolved. For shells that do not export `_`. Asynchronous, so a slow PATH entry (a network share) never blocks an ad request.
entries.title: CLI update: ad-client-context

ai.title: Terminal detection expanded with Zed, Tabby, Mintty, Konsole, GNOME
ai.summary: The CLI's ad client context now classifies additional Linux and Windows terminals by reading their environment variables (KONSOLE_VERSION, GNOME_TERMINAL_SCREEN, VTE_VERSION, XTERM_VERSION, WT_SESSION, GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR, ZED_TERM), and the common type vocabulary was extended to accept the new terminal and install-method enums. The detection is additive: a new out-of-vocabulary value drops the whole context rather than the single field, so clients and servers must both speak the new values, per a newly added warning in the schema file. A related refactor in ad-signals.ts replaced the raw-text extractor failedToolOutputText with shellFailureClassOf, which returns a classified error class instead of text, and resets lastErrorClass to 'none' on each turn start so stale errors do not ride later turns.
ai.evidence: Three files changed: cli/src/ads/ad-client-context.ts adds terminal detection for zed, tabby, mintty, conemu, windows_console, gnome_terminal, konsole, vte, xterm, foot and konsole via new environment variable reads (KONSOLE_VERSION, KONSOLE_DBUS_SESSION, GNOME_TERMINAL_SCREEN, GNOME_TERMINAL_SERVICE, VTE_VERSION, XTERM_VERSION, WT_SESSION, GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR, ZED_TERM); common/src/types/ad-client-context.ts adds the corresponding terminal enum values plus 'bunx' to INSTALL_METHODS and documents that vocabularies are additive-only (one out-of-range value drops the whole context); cli/src/ads/ad-signals.ts renames failedToolOutputText to shellFailureClassOf, which now returns an error class directly instead of raw text, and resets lastErrorClass to 'none' at each turn start.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show whether the server-side ad routes (/api/v1/ads, /api/ads) have been updated to accept the new vocabulary values, only that the schema warns they must be before a client sends them.

changes.what: Expanded terminal detection to identify zed, tabby, mintty, conemu, windows_console, gnome_terminal, konsole, vte, xterm, and foot from their environment variables, and read real launcher paths via getCliEnv().CODEBUFF_IS_BINARY.
Added the new terminal enum values and 'bunx' to INSTALL_METHODS, and documented that vocabularies are additive-only with one out-of-range value dropping the whole context.
Replaced failedToolOutputText with shellFailureClassOf, which returns an error class directly instead of raw text, and reset lastErrorClass to 'none' at each turn start.

eli5.text: The assistant's terminal recognition got smarter so it can now tell you're using Zed, Tabby, Mintty, Konsole, GNOME Terminal or a plain Windows console instead of lumping you in with every other unknown terminal. This is an internal change for the engineering team's testing and tracking, so it does not change how the assistant codes or what features you see. If you use one of those terminals you will simply be correctly identified in the logs, but there is no visible change to your daily workflow.

facts: Everything the root may spawn: pickers and searchers for context, the worker for slices. The code-searcher is programmatic — a batch of ripgrep queries and no model call — so it needs no free-mode allowlist entry.

What a worker may not run of base3's own tools: the terminal, because verification is the root's, once, for every slice together, and a worker with a terminal runs the suite N times in parallel; and the todo list, which is the root's plan. Everything else base3 has, the worker has.

Deliberately short and mostly suggestions: the agent answers questions, explores as long as it needs to, and decides when to split. What it is told firmly is the one thing it would otherwise skip (spawning helpers in parallel) and the one failure the fan-out invites (incoherent slices).
Drop the web tools, as createBase3CliRoot does for the eval harness.

Neither arm may read the public repository under evaluation off the web: read_url is refused by the bench, and a search result quoting its current code is the answer key. Both arms lose the two tools together.

A worker must be pinned to its root's model or the session gate rejects it mid-run, so the worker id names the model. Which models run this harness is FREEBUFF_FAST_MODE_MODEL_IDS (common/src/constants/freebuff-model-ids.ts).
